summary: Mississippi taxes construction by contract type: a 3.5% contractor's tax on non-residential prime contracts over $10,000; otherwise 7% on some trades and none on others.

conditions.when: Non-residential prime contract over $10,000: 3.5% contractor's tax on the total contract price, paid by the prime contractor

Residential, or $10,000 or less: plumbing, electrical, heating and air conditioning, excavating, landscaping, insulating, sheet metal and other services listed in Miss. Code Ann. 27-65-23 (7% on gross income)
Residential, or $10,000 or less: installed sales of roofing, tile, glass, carpet, fences, awnings or floor coverings by a dealer (7% on gross income)
Residential, or $10,000 or less: painting, drywall, masonry, carpentry, structural steel and other work not listed in 27-65-23 (no tax on the contract; contractor pays 7% on materials)

citations.title: MS DOR, Guide for Construction Contractors
citations.quote: The Sales Tax Law levies a 3.5% contractor's tax on all non-residential construction activities when the total contract price or compensation received exceeds $10,000.00.

citations.title: MS DOR, Guide for Construction Contractors
citations.quote: Residential construction (not including apartments or condominiums) is excluded from the 3.5% contractor's tax, but is subject to retail sales taxes.

citations.title: MS DOR, Guide for Construction Contractors (painting, drywall, masonry, carpentry, $10,000 and under or residential)
citations.quote: No sales tax on gross income. 7% sales or use tax on purchases of materials and services.

citations.title: MS DOR, Guide for Construction Contractors (plumbing, electrical, HVAC and other 27-65-23 trades)
citations.quote: 7% sales tax on gross income. No sales or use tax on purchases of component materials and services.

citations.title: MS DOR, Sales Tax Rates (27-65-23 services)
citations.quote: Plumbing or pipe fitting;

citations.title: Miss. Admin. Code 35.IV.10.01.201
citations.quote: Contracts for residential construction are not taxable under Miss. Code Ann. Section 27-65-21 and do not qualify for an MPC.

citations.title: Miss. Admin. Code 35.IV.10.01, revision note
citations.quote: 35.IV.10.01 revised effective April 1, 2018.

notes: Applies to new construction and repair alike ('erect, add to or repair'). Apartments and condominiums are non-residential for the contractor's tax. Whether local levies (Jackson, Tupelo) reach the 3.5% contractor's tax or the 7% trades is not read here. 2018-04-01 is the regulation's revision date.

summary: A delivery charge follows the tax treatment of the goods delivered in Mississippi, so it is exempt when the goods are exempt.

citations.title: Mississippi DOR fact sheet, Delivery Charges (revised October 2017; as of July 9, 2025)
citations.quote: Delivery charges are exempt if the product being shipped or delivered is exempt.

citations.title: Mississippi DOR fact sheet, Delivery Charges (revised October 2017; as of July 9, 2025)
citations.quote: The rate and application of sales or use tax on delivery charges follows the tax treatment of the property being shipped or delivered.

citations.title: Mississippi DOR, Sales Tax Rates
citations.quote: same rate as property being shipped.

notes: The fact sheet was on dor.ms.gov through at least July 2025 and returns 404 there on 2026-11-01; no replacement or contrary statement was found, so it is read from the Internet Archive copy. 2017-10-31 is the end of the month the sheet says it was revised. The rates-page quote concerns transportation charges paid directly by the consumer, and supports the same principle. Groceries are not exempt in Mississippi from 2025-07-01 (taxed at 5%); their delivery is not this code. No local levy applies where the state exempts the goods.

summary: A seller's delivery charge is part of taxable gross proceeds in Mississippi, even if separately stated.

citations.title: Miss. Admin. Code 35.IV.2.03.100 (Mileage, Delivery Charges and Rebilled Expenses)
citations.quote: This includes any charges made by the seller for delivery of property sold to the purchaser even though such amounts are separately stated on the seller's invoice apart from the sales price of the property.

citations.title: Miss. Admin. Code 35.IV.2.03, revision note
citations.quote: 35.IV.2.03 revised effective August 3, 2026

notes: 2026-08-03 is the date of the rule version archived; the earlier text wasn't read, though the treatment appears long-standing. Delivery of goods taxed at 5% (groceries) presumably takes the goods' rate (DOR rates page: transportation charges at the 'same rate as property being shipped'), unverified for seller-billed delivery. delivery.exempt_goods is not written: no official statement found.

The only local levies on general retail sales listed by the DOR are Jackson's 1% special infrastructure tax (activities taxed at 7% or more) and Tupelo's 0.25% water procurement tax (sales at the general rate; groceries added from 2026-05-01 by HB 4112). The many city tourism levies apply to restaurants, prepared food and hotels, not groceries. Groceries at 5% therefore fall outside local levies, except Tupelo's from 2026-05-01.

summary: Clothing and footwear, including accessories and protective or sporting gear, are taxable at the general sales-tax rate.

citations.title: MS DOR, Mississippi Sales and Use Taxes
citations.quote: All sales of tangible personal property in the State of Mississippi are subject to the regular retail rate of sales tax (7%) unless the law exempts the item or provides a reduced rate of tax for an item.

notes: Undated current agency page: 2018-01-01 uses the existing MS rule's convention for undated current sources, not a verified enactment date. General tangible-property rule covers subcodes; no permanent clothing price exemption found. The 2026 sales-tax holiday guide provides a temporary exemption for qualifying clothing and footwear under $100; holiday not modeled. General local sales-tax base differences were not stated on the sources read; MS rule covers general state/local parts. Separate local tourism or restaurant levies are not included.

summary: Packaged alcoholic beverages and drinks served at bars or restaurants are taxable at the general sales-tax rate.

citations.title: MS DOR, Sales Tax Rates — retail sales
citations.quote: Other tangible personal property including alcoholic beverages and beer ...... 7%

citations.title: Miss. Admin. Code 35.IV.9.02.101
citations.quote: The gross proceeds of sales by restaurants, cafes, cafeterias, snack bars, drive-ins, beer parlors, lounges, night clubs, concessions, caterers or other vendors of beverages and food products are taxable at the regular retail rate of tax.

notes: 2025-08-08 is the printed revision effective date of 35.IV.9.02, used as earliest verified, not a new tax. Rates page's 0% wholesale alcoholic-beverage line does not exempt retail sales. Separate alcohol excises/ABC charges and local restaurant/tourism levies are not included. General local base differences were not stated in the pages read.

summary: Rentals and leases of ordinary equipment, tools, furniture and party goods used in Mississippi are taxed at the general sales-tax rate, for fixed or indeterminate terms.

citations.title: Mississippi Administrative Code 35.IV.5.03.101, Renting or Leasing Tangible Personal Property
citations.quote: The tax due on the lease or rental is at the same rate as the sale of the property.

citations.title: Mississippi Administrative Code 35.IV.5.03.201, Rental or Lease
citations.quote: Rental or Lease means any transfer of possession or control of tangible personal property for a fixed or indeterminate term for consideration.

notes: Undated current DOR guidance uses 2018-01-01, the existing MS convention; this is not a verified enactment date. No term-length split for ordinary goods is stated. Specially rated or exempt underlying goods retain their treatment. Operator-and-crew services are outside rental. The regulation also describes a separate 6% short-term motor-vehicle rental tax, excluded from this code. General state/local convention follows existing MS rules; separate local tourism levies not modeled.

summary: Repair labor on tangible personal property is taxable in Mississippi, including ordinary auto and equipment repairs.

citations.title: Mississippi DOR, Business Tax Frequently Asked Questions, Is repair labor taxable?
citations.quote: Yes, repairs of tangible personal property are taxable.

notes: Undated current DOR guidance uses 2018-01-01, the existing MS convention; this is not a verified enactment date. The repair-labor FAQ imposes no separate-statement exception. Clothing alterations performed as part of laundry or cleaning are expressly taxable under 35.IV.5.02.103. Standalone tailoring/alteration treatment was not conclusively established; see gap. Separately stated parts are goods. General MS state/local convention follows existing rules.

citations.quote: Miss. Code Ann. Section 27-65-101(o) exempts the gross collections from self-service commercial laundering, drying, cleaning and pressing equipment.

citations.title: Mississippi Administrative Code 35.IV.5.09.100, Car Washes
citations.quote: Section 27-65-23 of the Mississippi sales tax law taxes car washing with an exemption provided in Section 27-65-111(x) for self-service, coin operated car washes and car washes performed using portable high pressure washing equipment when the service is performed on the premises of the customer.

notes: Date is the printed revision effective date of laundry chapter, used as earliest verified. Car-wash chapter is undated and uses existing MS undated-source convention. Staffed manual and mixed manual/automatic washes are taxable. General MS state/local convention follows existing rules.
